content: agent1 (TTL feature): I edit dspy/clients/cache.py (Cache.__init__ gets 'ttl: Optional[int] = None' as the LAST param after memory_max_entries; import TTLCache; memory cache uses TTLCache when ttl set; Cache.put uses disk_cache.set(expire=ttl); Cache.get calls disk_cache.expire() on miss) and dspy/clients/__init__.py (configure_cache gets 'ttl' as the LAST param after enable_litellm_cache; new set_ttl(seconds) helper; DSPY_CACHE ttl=None; 'set_ttl' added to __all__). What files/regions does your feature touch? If you add params to Cache.__init__/configure_cache, tell me so we agree on order.

agent1 = per-entry TTL (ttl param, TTLCache in memory, disk set(expire=ttl), expire() on get-miss, set_ttl helper). Proposal so our hunks do not touch adjacent lines (git conflicts on adjacent edits):
cache.py:
 1) imports: I change ONLY the line 'from cachetools import LRUCache' -> 'LRUCache, TTLCache'. Keep your imports (zlib etc.) in the stdlib block at the top, not next to the 3rd-party block.
 2) Cache.__init__ signature: you insert your params right AFTER 'memory_max_entries: Optional[int] = 1000000,'. I insert 'ttl: Optional[int] = None,' AFTER the existing blank line, just before '):' (one unchanged blank line separates us). Docstring: I add my ttl line BEFORE the 'memory_max_entries:' doc line; you append yours after it.
 3) __init__ body: I rewrite only the memory block (the 'if self.enable_memory_cache: ... self.memory_cache = {}' lines) and add 'self.ttl = ttl' as the LAST statement after 'self._lock = threading.RLock()'. You: add your attrs elsewhere (top of body / inside FanoutCache(...) args), not in the memory block and not after self._lock.
 4) get(): I only change the 'else:\n            return None' branch (add disk_cache.expire() when ttl is set). You change 'response = self.disk_cache[key]' as you like.
 5) put() (the one real collision): please do NOT edit the line 'self.disk_cache[key] = value'. I replace it with 'if self.ttl is not None: self.disk_cache.set(key, value, expire=self.ttl) else: self.disk_cache[key] = value'. For compression, rebind the value BEFORE the 'try:' (between 'if self.enable_disk_cache:' and 'try:'): 'value = self._encode(value)' (memory write already happened above, so rebinding is safe). Make _encode not raise (fall back to the raw value) since it sits outside the try.
 6) I add a new method 'set_ttl' at the very END of class Cache (after load_memory_cache); put your helpers (_encode/_decode) elsewhere, e.g. right after __init__.
__init__.py:
 7) configure_cache signature: you insert your params right AFTER 'memory_max_entries: Optional[int] = 1000000,' (before enable_litellm_cache); I append 'ttl: Optional[int] = None,' AFTER 'enable_litellm_cache: bool = False,'. Same for the docstring (mine last, after the enable_litellm_cache line).
 8) the Cache(...) call in configure_cache and DSPY_CACHE(...): additive kwargs; I add 'ttl=ttl,' / 'ttl=None,' as the LAST kwarg; you add yours right after 'memory_max_entries' (they will be adjacent, fine, both are pure additions).
 9) __all__: I insert '"set_ttl",' BETWEEN '"disable_litellm_logging",' and '"configure_cache",'; you append yours AFTER '"configure_cache",'.
 10) set_ttl() function: I put it right AFTER the DSPY_CACHE = Cache(...) block (before the '# Turn off by default' comment); put set_compression() elsewhere (e.g. right after configure_cache, before 'litellm.telemetry = False').
At the end, send me your 'git diff' text and I send mine, and we each check the two apply cleanly together. OK?

agent1: my TTL edits are done in my workspace and follow our agreed slots.
